key_insight: Decouple cache hits from correctness by returning optimistic cached responses immediately and verifying them asynchronously, enabling higher semantic-cache hit rates in tiered static/dynamic LLM caches without sacrificing response fidelity.
problem_solved: Production tiered semantic caches use a single embedding-similarity threshold, forcing a tradeoff between conservative thresholds (low hits, high safety) and permissive thresholds (high hits, noisy/unsafe responses). The paper solves how to increase hit rates while still ensuring cached responses are verified and trustworthy.
method: Serve optimistic hits from static/dynamic tiers immediately when similarity passes a permissive threshold, then verify correctness asynchronously using lightweight verifiers or validation checks.

If asynchronous verification fails, revoke or replace the cached response and optionally re-request a fresh LLM inference; apply tier-aware policies (e.g., stricter static cache rules, adaptive thresholds for dynamic cache).
Maintain correctness metadata and verification state so the system can audit, roll back, or refresh cached entries without blocking user-facing latency.
impact: Enables production LLM systems to substantially reduce latency and inference cost while preserving response quality and safety—making semantic caching practical at higher hit rates for search, assistants, and agent workflows.
visual_elements: Flow diagram of tiered cache: static cache + dynamic cache → optimistic serve → asynchronous verifier → revoke/refresh loop
Timeline illustrating instant response vs background verification (showing no user-facing latency impact)
Tradeoff plot: single-threshold (accuracy vs hit-rate) vs asynchronous-verified approach shifting curve toward higher hit-rate without accuracy loss
Before/after bar chart of latency and cost per request comparing traditional single-threshold cache vs asynchronous verified caching
paper_title: Asynchronous Verified Semantic Caching for Tiered LLM Architectures
paper_authors: Asmit Kumar Singh, Haozhe Wang, Laxmi Naga Santosh Attaluri, Tak Chiam, Weihua Zhu
